doc.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Finding your own voice amid many influences
summary: Nussbaum says he is a product of classical music, rock, Motown and Hendrix before jazz, and draws on many influences including non-musical ones.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Do you think it ever gets to the point where, does it get harder to have your own voice because there’s so many more people that have come before you?

I think that as time goes on we have to realize that nobody can be, like nobody can be me better than me. And I have to tap into all my different influences and I am my own person. And the way I look at things and the way that I am establishes and helps to shape what I’m about. I have a multitude of influences. I mean who said that great line, it’s like to steal from one person is plagiarism, to steal from many is research. And that’s kind of what I’ve done. I mean I’m a product of my time. I didn’t grow up playing bebop, I grew up listening to classical music and playing rock & roll. So that’s all part of my roots, that’s part of my Wonder Bread years. So I can’t deny the fact that I was effected by Jimi Hendrix, that I love Motown, that I used to listen to Bartok and opera when I was a child. That’s all part of me. So then I did a whole study of learning about jazz, my own pursuit, because I loved it, and I’m really somebody who’s interested in the history of it that all these things kind of effect me. I mean certain people I love their sound, I don’t dig their feel. Certain people I like their swing, but I don’t really get much from the — you know I’ve taken different things from different people and not just drummers or musicians. Other influences of people in the arts and things like that have effected me. You know, visual things that I see. Being up here in the rolling hills influences how I think about things. Watching the clouds in the sky, an ice skater, all those things kind of effect my aesthetic viewpoint, which effects me.
